subtype: Approach: handling a negative comment by pausing [Revision]
passage: The comment said my drawing looked like a kindergarten project, from an account with a blank profile picture. My face went hot and my fingers were already typing something nasty. I'm Tushar, and I want to tell you what I did instead: I put the phone in the other room for one hour. I ate a banana and walked around the block. After the hour, the reply I'd wanted to write sounded silly, even to me. So I ignored it, deleted the comment and blocked the account. Then I texted Rukmini, who calls me bhai: “Someone was mean online, feeling weird.” She sent back, “Want to call?” We talked for ten minutes. No argument, no audience, and by dinner my drawing looked fine again.

qa.q: How long did Tushar wait before deciding what to do?
qa.a: Tushar put the phone in the other room for one hour.

qa.q: What was Tushar feeling when he read the comment?
qa.a: Tushar felt hurt and angry, since his face went hot and he started typing something nasty.

qa.q: What could Tushar do if the comments keep coming?
qa.a: Tushar could report the account and tell a trusted adult, since repeated meanness is not something to handle alone.

qa.q: How might Rukmini feel on receiving the text?
qa.a: Rukmini probably feels concerned and glad that Tushar reached out, since she answers at once and offers a call.

grounding: After a mean comment, a teen waits an hour, decides to ignore it, deletes and blocks, and later checks in with a friend instead of arguing.

subtype: Approach: handling a negative comment by pausing [Revision]
passage:
I'm Nirmala, and I was sitting with Jahnavi on the school bus when the comment came in under her dance video: “lol who told you that you can dance.” I saw her face drop. Her thumbs were already moving to reply.
Then she stopped, locked the phone and put it in her bag. “Not now,” she said, mostly to herself. “An hour.”
She talked to me about the maths test for the rest of the ride, though she kept glancing at the bag. At home, about an hour later, she messaged me: “Checked again. Not replying. It's someone I don't even know.” She had deleted the comment and blocked the account.
That evening she called me, just to talk. She asked if I thought the video was bad. I said no, and meant it. She laughed a little and said she would post the next one anyway.
I don't know what she'd have typed on the bus. I'm glad she didn't.

qa.a: lol who told you that you can dance.

qa.q: How did Jahnavi feel when she first saw the comment?
qa.a: Jahnavi was hurt, her face dropping, and her first urge was to fire back a reply.

qa.q: What else could Jahnavi do if more mean comments come?
qa.a: Keep the same pause, delete and block, and tell a parent or teacher if it turns into repeated targeting.

qa.q: What was it like for Nirmala to get that evening call?
qa.a: Nirmala felt trusted to reassure a friend, and meant it when saying the video wasn't bad.

grounding: A friend sees a teen pause an hour before replying to a mean comment, then delete and block it, and later check in with a friend rather than argue.

subtype: Approach: handling a negative comment by pausing [Revision]
passage:
Saturday, 6 pm: Aditi posts a photo from her first painting exhibition at the community hall. At 6:40 a comment appears: “Kindergarten art.” Her heart pounds. She types a sharp reply, then remembers her own rule: no replies for an hour when upset. She puts the phone face down.
Saturday, 7:45 pm: She reads it again. It's an account with no photo and twelve followers. Replying would only give it attention. She deletes the comment and blocks the account.
Saturday, 9 pm: She calls Tenzin, who was at the exhibition. “Was it really that bad?” Tenzin says the mountain painting was the best one there and bought a postcard of it. Aditi laughs for the first time that evening.
Sunday: Aditi posts a second photo, of the mountain painting, and turns on the setting that hides offensive comments.

qa.q: At what time did the mean comment appear?
How did Aditi feel when she first saw the comment?
qa.a: Aditi felt hurt and angry, heart pounding, and wanted to reply sharply.

qa.q: What else could Aditi do if the same person keeps making new accounts to comment?
qa.a: Keep deleting and blocking, and tell a parent or trusted adult so they can help report it.

qa.q: How might Tenzin feel getting the call?
qa.a: Tenzin is happy to reassure a friend and genuinely proud of the mountain painting.

grounding: Shows a teen waiting an hour before responding to a mean comment, deciding to ignore it, deleting and blocking, and later checking in with a friend.
